thread:
incident-bot: PROD alert — elevated 502 errors from the inference gateway (path /v1/generate). Paging @kara (oncall) and @jamal (sre). HTTP 502 spike started ~10:21 UTC. :rotating_light:

kara (oncall): on it — ACK. grabbing logs and traffic graph.

jamal (sre): I see increased 502s with upstream timeouts to runtime pool rwd-gpu-12. Starting remediation runbook.

kara (oncall): quick mitigation: I'm toggling fallback policy to model-variant small-1 for non-enterprise routes to reduce load. Will monitor.

ben (eng): thx. any idea if this is model or infra? I'm seeing RPC timeouts from runtime to model-worker on GPU node 7.

jamal (sre): same. hitting long GC / worker stalls on node7; kernel-level OOM look suspicious. marking node7 as draining.

ops-bot: autoscale policy triggered — spinning up 3 more inference instances (type p4d). Expected ready ~3m.

elaine (support): Heads up — a customer (Acme Corp) reported degraded experience via smart-sla alert. They saw failed requests in prod. Do we have a customer-facing blurb?

marta (cs): Need a short note for Acme: what to say about impact/duration and ETA for resolution.

kara (oncall): drafting status page update. Quick draft below — please review/shorten: 

```
Status update (investigating): At 10:21 UTC we detected elevated 502 errors affecting text generation requests. Traffic is partially degraded for some customers; requests are intermittently failing. Engineering is actively investigating and scaling capacity. We'll post another update within 30 minutes. 
```

jamal (sre): change "some customers" -> "a subset of customers using larger model variants and high-concurrency routes". Also include mitigation: "We have enabled automatic fallback to smaller model variants and added capacity".

marta (cs): LGTM. Add: "No customer data was exposed; this was a runtime availability issue."

kara (oncall): updated draft and pushing to status page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1801234567 (placeholder).

ops-bot: deploy/scale completed: 3 new instances healthy. 

jamal (sre): post-scale numbers: 502 rate dropped by ~70% after drain and scale. Latency back to normal for low-concurrency routes. Higher-concurrency requests still see intermittent failures, likely due to KV cache thrash on warmed nodes.

ben (eng): investigating cache eviction pattern; suspect mis-sized cache after last config change. Rolling a config tweak to increase KV cache per-worker by 25% to prevent evictions. Will apply to a canary set first.

kara (oncall): going to hand off to jamal for overnight ops. jamal, can you take lead for the next hour? I'll update the on-call rotation in the handoff note.

jamal (sre): taking it. Handoff note: scaled up + drained node7 + fallback to small-1 for non-enterprise -> monitoring. Next steps: observe for 60m, then revert fallback if stable, follow up on KV cache config.

elaine (support): Drafting customer notification for impacted tenants. Short email: 

```
Hi —

We saw intermittent request failures (HTTP 502) for some generation requests between ~10:21–11:05 UTC. Our team mitigated the issue by adding capacity and enabling automatic model fallbacks; most traffic returned to normal by 10:40 UTC and residual errors cleared by ~11:05 UTC. No customer data was exposed. We apologize for the disruption. If you experienced continued issues, please reply and we'll prioritize follow-up.

— Redwood Support
```

marta (cs): good. add a note that enterprise customers wanting SLA credits should open a ticket.

kara (oncall): jamal — please confirm when stable and post final status page "resolved" with a 1-paragraph summary for the public incident record.

jamal (sre): Will do. Current metrics: 502s per minute down to baseline, p95 latency stable. Setting timers to re-evaluate at +60m.

ops-bot: incident-timer set by jamal for 60m.

--- (one hour later) ---

jamal (sre): final check-in. System stable for 45m. Rolling back fallback for non-enterprise routes now to restore normal model routing.

ben (eng): KV cache config rollouts completed to 10% canary, healthy. Planning full rollout in 30m after monitoring.

kara (oncall): posting "resolved" on status page with short RCA. Draft RCA summary below for customer follow-up and public page: please edit.

```
RCA summary (public):

Impact: Between 10:21 and 11:05 UTC, a subset of generation requests experienced intermittent 502 errors and increased latency. Root cause: an unexpected worker-level memory pressure and KV cache eviction pattern on a GPU runtime node after a recent cache sizing change, which caused upstream timeouts and increased error rates for high-concurrency model variants. Mitigation: We drained the affected node, scaled additional inference capacity, temporarily enabled fallback to smaller model variants, and rolled a KV cache sizing fix. Full service was restored by 11:05 UTC. Preventative actions: revert risky cache sizing change in the next patch, add pre-deploy canary for cache metrics, update runbook to detect similar memory pressure earlier, and add automated fallback tests to CI.

Customer-impact note: Customers using large-model high-concurrency routes may have experienced failed or delayed requests. No customer data was accessed or leaked.
```

marta (cs): That reads well. For customers we're sending an internal-friendly RCA that includes timeline. I'll add a timeline section and send to Acme and any other impacted customers.

elaine (support): please include contact link for SLA inquiries. I'll prepare the outbound messages and CC engineering for technical follow-ups.

jamal (sre): creating a short internal timeline to attach: 

- 10:21 UTC: 502 spike detected by incident-bot.
- 10:23 UTC: oncall acknowledged, began investigation.
- 10:30 UTC: determined node7 memory pressure; started draining node.
- 10:33 UTC: enabled fallback to smaller model variants for non-enterprise routes.
- 10:36 UTC: autoscale added capacity (3 instances) — instances healthy by 10:40 UTC.
- 10:40–11:05 UTC: progressive reduction in 502s; config rollouts for KV cache fix started at 10:50 UTC.
- 11:05 UTC: residual errors cleared; monitoring for instability.

kara (oncall): thanks. jamal, can you own the postmortem doc? I'll add the incident timeline to oncall notes and close the page after your PM.

jamal (sre): taking postmortem ownership. I'll draft the technical RCA, assign action owners: ben for cache sizing rollback, eng infra to add canary checks, and ops to add earlier memory pressure alerts. ETA for draft: 48h.

marta (cs): As soon as internal RCA is ready, I'll send tailored follow-ups to impacted accounts and include the timeline and preventative steps.

elaine (support): sending outbound to Acme now (copying draft above). Will flag for SLA ticket if requested.

ben (eng): will open PR to revert cache sizing change and include a benchmark for cache eviction rates.

kara (oncall): closing loop — final status page updated to "resolved" and linked to postmortem placeholder. Great job team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident 1801234567 marked resolved by kara (oncall) at 11:12 UTC.

marta (cs): note for customer follow-up pack: short public summary, internal timeline, technical RCA (ben/jamal), and action owners + ETA. I'll collate and send updates to impacted customers once jamal shares the postmortem draft.

--- end thread ---
